rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drew out the angels’ concealed self-admiration in their worship, making them disclose their hidden thoughts by citing their glorification.
rows.anchor: استخرج الحق سبحانه منهم ما استكن في قلوبهم من استعظام طاعاتهم والملاحظة إلى أفعالهم بهذا الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is a greater merit than action: the angels had more and earlier worship, while Adam had more knowledge, which established his rank.
rows.anchor: الفضيلة بالعلم أتم من الفضيلة بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s answer that He knows what the angels do not know refers to His forgiveness of Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: من غفراني لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ glorification displays their deeds and merit, while forgiveness of human sins displays the Creator’s generosity and mercy.
rows.anchor: في تسبيحهم إظهار فعلهم واشتهار خصائصهم وفضلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no worship; their glorification establishes their own praise, while His forgiveness establishes the Creator’s praise.
rows.anchor: والحق سبحانه غني عن طاعات كل مطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the believers’ pure beliefs and keen inward protection of their covenantal love, even when disobedience stains their outward state.
rows.anchor: من صفاء عقائد المؤمنين منهم في محبتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows His love for them and the inward secrets He hides in them, unlike angels who openly display their states.
rows.anchor: وأنا أخفي عليهم أسراري فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows humans’ humbled, broken hearts despite their bad deeds, whereas angels’ hearts become proud when they display glorification.
rows.anchor: من انكسار قلوبهم وإن ارتكبوا قبيح أفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brokenness of servants’ hearts carries powerful standing with God, despite their outwardly disobedient condition.
rows.anchor: وإن لانكسار قلوب العباد عندنا لذماما قويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angelic glorification has no significance without God’s favor, and human sins cause no harm when met by His pardon.
rows.anchor: أي خطر لتسبيحكم لولا فضلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clothed the angels in obedience and purification, but clothed humans in pardon, mercy, generosity, and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: لبستكم طاعتكم ولبستهم رحمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God’s protection made the angels fortunate, His mercy has also reached human beings.
rows.anchor: إن أسعدتكم عصمتي فلقد أدركتهم رحمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ goodness is secured by infallibility, while human wrongdoers are immersed in mercy.
rows.anchor: لئن كان محسنكم عتيق العصمة فإن مجرمهم غريق الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ reliance on God purified their state and led them to admit ignorance, disclaiming all knowledge beyond what He gave them.
rows.anchor: اتكالهم علي زكى أحوالهم فألجأهم إلى الاعتراف بالجهالة حتى يتبرأوا عن المعارف إلا بمقدار ما من به الحق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic plural ‘the names’ implies all names, and ‘all of them’ reinforces their comprehensiveness and certainty.
rows.anchor: عموم قوله الأسماء يقتضي الاستغراق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes say Adam was taught the names of all created things.
rows.anchor: على ما نطق به تفسير ابن عباس وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was also taught God’s names, but God demonstrated his advantage to the angels through the created names.
rows.anchor: علمه أسماء الحق سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s exclusive knowledge of His own names is a secret disclosed to no angel, even one brought near.
rows.anchor: فذلك سر لم يطلع عليه ملك مقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One unable to equal Adam in knowing created names has no hope of approaching his knowledge of God’s names or the unseen.
rows.anchor: ومن ليس له رتبة مساواة آدم في معرفة أسماء المخلوقات فأي طمع في مداناته في أسماء الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If knowledge of created names warrants the angels’ prostration, the distinction in divine names warrants an even greater honor.
rows.anchor: فما الظن بالتخصيص بمعرفة أسماء الحق سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels’ specialty is glorification and purification, creaturely acts of worship; knowledge is a greater praiseworthy attribute associated with God.
rows.anchor: خصوصية الملائكة بالتسبيح والتقديس وهذه طاعات تليق بالمخلوقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God honored Adam secretly by teaching him, then publicly by demonstrating his distinction and giving him precedence.
rows.anchor: أكرمه في السر بما علمه ثم بين تخصيصه يوم الجهر وقدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay in ‘then He presented them’ may mean Adam was given time to settle and verify the knowledge in his heart before being questioned.
rows.anchor: فإنه أمهله من الوقت ما تقررذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the delay concerns the angels: they were asked abruptly without prior teaching, while Adam answered because he had already been taught.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم على وجه الوهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge ‘if you are truthful’ alludes to the angels’ claim of special standing and superiority over Adam; merit comes from prior divine choice, not earlier glorification.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أنهم تعرضوا لدعوى الخصوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking the angels to name what He knew they could not, God demonstrated His sovereign right to command and rule.
rows.anchor: ولما علم الحق سبحانه تقاصر علومهم عن معرفة أسماء المخلوقات ثم كلفهم الإنباء عنها صار فيه أوضح دلالة على أن الأمر أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine rulings are not governed by human claims about rationally attractive outcomes; God may obligate whom He wills, and good or bad is what He judges so.
rows.anchor: ردا على من توهم أن أحكام الحق سبحانه معللة باستحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels praised God before excusing themselves, acknowledging they lacked the requested knowledge and that no one may blame Him for testing the unable.
rows.anchor: قدموا الثناء على ذكر ما اعتذروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God All-Knowing and Wise affirms that whatever He does is true and right, beyond anyone’s judgment and free of folly or wrong.
rows.anchor: إنك أنت العليم الحكيم أي ما تفعله فهو حق صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant is preserving knowledge of Him; the servant’s covenant is receiving forgiveness.
rows.anchor: حفظ المعرفة وعهدنا اتصال المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant is guarding what He loves; its fulfillment is His subtle reward.
rows.anchor: عهده حفظ محابه وعهدنا لطف ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant is remaining present at His door, and His fulfillment is abundant return.
rows.anchor: عهده حضور الباب وعهدنا جزيل المآب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping the covenant means guarding the secret; God fulfills it with beautiful righteousness.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بحفظ السر أوف بعهدكم بجميل البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human pledge was accepted on the day of the primordial covenant, and God’s response is promised on the day of return.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي الذي قبلتم يوم الميثاق أوف بعهدكم الذي ضمنت لكم يوم التلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant must prefer no one over God, and God will not withhold His kindness or good.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في ألا تؤثروا علي غيري أوف بعهدكم في ألا أمنع عنكم لطفي وخيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Servants keep the covenant by caring for the trusts planted within them; God fulfills it through enduring flashes of illumination.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي برعاية ما أثبت فيكم من الودائع أوف بعهدكم بما أديم لكم من شوارق اللوامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preserving God’s secrets is answered by His beautiful recompense.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بحفظ أسراري أوف بعهدكم بجميل مباري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sustaining knowledge of God is answered by the continued renewal of His beneficence.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي باستدامة عرفاني أوف بعهدكم في إدامة إحساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Serving God is answered by His favor in accepting that service.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في القيام بخدمتي أوف بعهدكم في المنة عليكم بقبولها منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good spiritual striving and conduct are answered by lasting communion and direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في القيام بحسن المجاهدة والمعاملة أوف بعهدكم بدوام المواصلة والمشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disclaiming one’s own power and merit is answered by God’s abundant favor and generosity.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بالتبري عن الحول والمنة أوف بعهدكم بالإكرام بالطول والمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant asks for preference and reliance; God fulfills it by sufficiency and favor.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بالتفضيل والتوكل أوف بعهدكم بالكفاية والتفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere love is answered by complete nearness to God.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بصدق المحبة أوف بعهدكم بكمال القربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being satisfied with God alone is answered by God’s being satisfied with the servants.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي اكتفوا مني بي أوف بعهدكم أرضي بكم عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the realm of absence, servants obey and exert themselves in service; in proximity, God grants intimacy, vision, His address, and perfect nearness.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في دار الغيبة على بساط الخدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving up desires in response to spiritual demands is met by God’s sufficing the servants in those demands.
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في المطالبات بترك الشهوات أوف بعهدكم بكفايتكم تلك المطالبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant continually says ‘My Lord,’ and God answers by addressing the servant as ‘My servant.’
rows.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بأن تقولوا أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear God alone, since only He has power to create; no one without power or favor is rightly feared.
rows.anchor: أي أفردوني بالخشية لانفرادي بالقدرة على الإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant should join faith grounded in revelation with faith grounded in proof; common believers reason inferentially, the elite turn to revelation, and the elite of the elite reach direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: إشارة أن يقرن ( العبد ) إيمانه من حيث البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not become the first disbeliever or establish disbelief as a precedent, since an innovator bears more blame than later followers.
rows.anchor: ولا تسنوا الكفر سنة فإن وزر المبتدئ فيما يسن أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exchange God’s signs for a small price: do not prefer a trivial personal benefit over His immense right.
rows.anchor: لا تؤثروا على عظيم حقي خسيس حظكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many fear God’s punishment, but few are in awe of His seeing and knowing them.
rows.anchor: كثير من يتقي عقوبته وعزيز من يهاب اطلاعه ورؤيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant cannot occupy two contrary states at once: either expanded through God or bound by self-interest.
rows.anchor: لا تتوهموا أن يلتئم لكم جمع الضدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those drawn away from their own witness differ from those veiled within it; people of nearness and connection do not resemble people of separation and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: المجذوب عن شاهده كالمحجوب في شاهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elect’s inherited favor is unlike the state of those driven away by divine severity.
rows.anchor: وعتيق فضلنا لا يشبه طريد قهرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers’ insight is impaired: they see no correctness in believers’ affairs, disapprove of them, and respond to each new event with a new objection.
rows.anchor: سقمت بصائر الكفار فلم يلح لهم وجه الصواب في جميع أحوال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the qibla changed to the Kaaba, objectors asked why the believers had turned away if their previous direction was true.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك تغير أمر القبلة حينما حولت إلى الكعبة قالوا إن كانت قبلتهم حقا فما الذي ولاهم عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns east and west and directs worshippers toward whichever direction He wills.
rows.anchor: يتعبد العباد إلى قطر و ( . . . ) ونحو شاؤوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People veiled from witnessing God’s direction of His saints seek rational explanations for their states; seeing all from one perspective would end divided thought and doubt.
rows.anchor: عن شهود تصريف الحق لأوليائه - يطلبون وجوها من الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides whomever He wills to His light.
rows.anchor: ولكن الله يهدي لنوره من شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Middle’ means best: God made this community the best of nations and the Sufi elect the best of this community, the best of the best.
rows.anchor: فجعل هذه الأمة خيار الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as the community witnesses over other nations at the Resurrection, the Sufi elect are its foundation and pivot, through whom God preserves the whole community.
rows.anchor: فكما أن هذه الأمة شهداء على الأمم في القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever the elect’s hearts accept is accepted, and whoever they reject is rejected.
rows.anchor: وكل من قبلته قلوبهم فهو المقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protects the community from collective error and protects the elect from error in insight, judgment, acceptance, and rejection.
rows.anchor: وعصم هذه الطائفة عن الخطأ في النظر والحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elect’s judgments rest on the Prophet’s practice; anything without prophetic following is rejected and its adherent has no standing.
rows.anchor: ثم إن بناء أمرهم مستند إلى سنة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporary qibla and its change tested the community, distinguishing truthful followers from apostates; division makes the change seem difficult, while reality reveals its correctness.
rows.anchor: كان اختبارا لهم من الحق ليتميز الصادق من المارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those with one heart toward God, changing circumstances are equivalent: whether God changes or confirms a matter, their relation to Him remains one.
rows.anchor: من كان مع الله في جميع الأحوال على قلب واحد فالمختلفات من الأحوال له واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poet portrays the steadfast lover as turning with the glass wherever it turns, though onlookers think the lover mad.
rows.anchor: كيفما دارت الزجاجة درنا . . . يحسب الجاهلون أنا جننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facing east or west, stone or earthen clod, does not change the heart’s single aim; what is for the One has one ruling in every state.
rows.anchor: فإن قابلوا شرقا أو واجهوا غربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet maintained proper etiquette by not voicing his heart’s wish for a changed qibla, while looking toward heaven as the route of Gabriel.
rows.anchor: حفظ - صلوات الله عليه - الآداب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew the Prophet’s unspoken request and changed the qibla for him, describing this as the greatest act a beloved can receive from the Beloved.
rows.anchor: أي علمنا سؤلك عما لم تفصح عنه بلسان الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone else strives to win God’s pleasure, while God seeks the Prophet’s pleasure by giving him a qibla he likes.
rows.anchor: كل العبيد يجتهدون في طلب رضائي وأنا أطلب رضاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should face the Kaaba outwardly without attaching their hearts to stones or relics; God alone should be the heart’s witness.
rows.anchor: ولكن لا تعلق قلبك بالأحجار والآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are likewise commanded to face the qibla while purifying their hearts for God and directing their witnessing to Him alone.
rows.anchor: ولكن أخلصوا قلوبكم لي وأفردوا شهودكم بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scriptural knowledge of the People of the Book gives them no proof, relief, or benefit; God’s warning frightens enemies and reassures friends.
rows.anchor: ولكنه علم لا يكون عليهم حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God’s primordial decree, the People of the Book will not follow the believers’ qibla despite manifest signs, and the Prophet will not follow theirs despite their stratagems.
rows.anchor: فما هم بتابعي قبلتكم وإن أريتهم من الآثار ما هو أظهر من الشموس والأقمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God entails becoming consumed in His presence, after which He remembers the servant once the servant has vanished from selfhood.
rows.anchor: أي كونوا مستهلكين في وجودنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the earlier description of the virtuous as people who existed for a moment yet were permanently absent from themselves.
rows.anchor: كانوا وقتا ولكنهم بانوا دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the people of outward expression, remembering means conformity and God’s remembrance means bestowed honors.
rows.anchor: وطريقة أهل العبارة { فاذكروني } بالموافقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the people of inward allusion, remembrance means abandoning every self-interest, and God’s response is to establish them through Him after self-annihilation.
rows.anchor: وطريقة أهل الإشارة { فاذكروني } بترك كل حظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be content with God instead of His gifts and favors; He remembers you by being satisfied with you apart from your deeds.
rows.anchor: { فاذكروني } مكتفين بي عن عطائي وأفضالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant’s later remembrance depends on God’s prior remembrance; without the prior divine act, the servant could not remember.
rows.anchor: ولولا سابق ذكري لما كان لاحق ذكركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting off attachments is answered by God’s remembrance through the qualities of spiritual realities.
rows.anchor: بقطع العلائق { أذكركم } بنعوت الحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God among those you meet, and He will remember you among those He addresses, as the cited report promises.
rows.anchor: فمن ذكرني في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant should thank God for the great favor of commanding, ‘Remember Me, and I will remember you.’
rows.anchor: على عظيم المنة عليكم بأن قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is remembrance, and the prohibition on ingratitude is a command to thank God; repeating remembrance emphasizes abundant practice.
rows.anchor: النهي عن الكفران أمر بالشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because lovers often mention what they love, the command to remember God much is truly a command to love Him, with His love answering theirs.
rows.anchor: أمر بالمحبة أي أحببني أحبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God in humility is answered by His gracious favor.
rows.anchor: بالتذلل { أذكركم } بالتفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering through brokenness is answered by God’s blessing.
rows.anchor: بالانكسار { أذكركم } بالمبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering with the tongue is answered by God’s remembrance in the heart.
rows.anchor: باللسان { أذكركم } بالجنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering with the heart is answered by fulfillment of the servant’s goal.
rows.anchor: بقلوبكم { أذكركم } بتحقيق مطلوبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Serving at God’s door is answered by acceptance at the ground of nearness and completion of grace.
rows.anchor: على الباب من حيث الخدمة { أذكركم } بالإيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying the inward secret is answered by God’s completion of righteousness.
rows.anchor: بتصفية السر { أذكركم } بتوفية البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance through effort and hardship is answered by divine generosity and giving.
rows.anchor: بالجهد والعناء { أذكركم } بالجود والعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering in a state of safety is answered by God’s remembrance on Resurrection Day, when regret no longer helps.
rows.anchor: بوصف السلامة { أذكركم } يوم القيامة يوم لا تنفع الندامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God through fear is answered by the realization of desire.
rows.anchor: بالرهبة { أذكركم } بتحقيق الرغبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience under the unfolding of God’s decrees in prayer earns the Lord’s blessings, as the following verse says of the patient.
rows.anchor: استعينوا بالصبر على الصلاة أي بصبركم - عند جريان أحكام الحق عليكم - استحقاقكم صلاة ربكم عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient deserve the highest treasure and rank because they attain God’s companionship.
rows.anchor: وعلو القدر حيث نالوا معية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s companionship with the patient is explicitly affirmed by the cited verse.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { إن الله مع الصابرين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever opposes one’s desire and removes one from ease and attraction is more correct in itself.
rows.anchor: وكل ما كان إلى خلاف هواك أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing are those who prefer God’s approval over their own desires; when they act for Him, He supports them.
rows.anchor: الذين اتقوا إيثار هواهم على ما فيه رضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealthy people spend money, worshippers spend themselves in duties, gnostics spend their hearts in obedience, and lovers spend their spirits in love.
rows.anchor: إنفاق الأغنياء من أموالهم ، وإنفاق العابدين بنفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy spend material blessings, while the poor spend their spiritual aspirations.
rows.anchor: إنفاق الأغنياء من النعم وإنفاق الفقراء من الهمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy give money from their purses, the poor give their most precious lives, and monotheists remove creation from their innermost secrets.
rows.anchor: إنفاق الأغنياء إخراج المال من الكيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Casting oneself into destruction means withholding one’s hand from giving and saving something for oneself.
rows.anchor: الإشارة فيه إلى إمساك يدك عن البذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction also means preferring one’s desire over God’s approval.
rows.anchor: ويقال : إلى إيثار هواك على رضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction can mean deliberately choosing to be heedless of God.
rows.anchor: { ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة } أي الغفلة عنه بالاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is destructive to imagine one can live even a moment without God’s kindness and attention.
rows.anchor: توهم أنك تعيش من دون لطفه وإقباله لحظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting one’s own spiritual slackness and veiling is another form of destruction.
rows.anchor: الرضا بما أنت فيه من الفترة والحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction also includes refraining from continual supplication for help with every breath.
rows.anchor: إمساك اللسان عن دوام الاستغاثة في كل نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual excellence is kindness to everyone except oneself: reliance on oneself harms the self by making it undertake and endure every hardship.
rows.anchor: الإحسان أن ترفق مع كل أحد إلا معك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excellence also means relinquishing every personal interest completely.
rows.anchor: والإحسان أيضا ترك جميع حظوظك من غير بقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excellence also means devoting oneself to fulfilling every person’s right one is responsible for.
rows.anchor: والإحسان أيضا تفرغك إلى قضاء حق كل أحد علق عليك حديثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excellence is worshipping God without heedlessness.
rows.anchor: والإحسان أن تعبده على غير غفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excellence is worshipping God with direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: والإحسان أن تعبده وأنت بوصف المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, completing pilgrimage means observing its pillars, Sunnas, and prescribed forms, including sacrifice, without neglecting any aspect.
rows.anchor: إتمام الحج على لسان العلم القيام بأركانه وسننه وهيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited exegesis says one should enter ihram for both pilgrimage and umrah from one’s home.
rows.anchor: وفي التفسير أن تحرم بهما من دويرة أهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In inward interpretation, pilgrimage is intention: aiming at the House is the commoners’ pilgrimage, while aiming at God is the elect’s pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وعلى لسان الإشارة الحج هو القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart’s pilgrimage begins with sound commitment and clear intent, then sheds disobedience and desire, takes on patience and poverty, and resists appetite and vain hopes.
rows.anchor: فإحرامه بعقد صحيح على قصد صريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bodily pilgrim appears dusty and disheveled in humility; inwardly, every part of the heart answers God’s call.
rows.anchor: ثم الحاج أشعث أغبر تظهر عليه آثار الخشوع والخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best pilgrimage combines blood sacrifice and loud talbiya; inwardly this means shedding the ego through resistance and raising the secret’s voice in constant supplication and response.
rows.anchor: الشج صب الدم والعج رفع الصوت بالتلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing at the courts of nearness means completing the qualities of reverent awe.
rows.anchor: ثم الوقوف بساحات القربة باستكمال أوصاف الهيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Souls stand at Arafat; hearts stand among the names and attributes, before the majesty of the Essence in communion.
rows.anchor: وموقف النفوس عرفات وموقف القلوب الأسامي والصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward rites are the hearts’ circumambulation around witnessing majesty and the secrets’ movement between disclosure of majesty and gentleness of beauty.
rows.anchor: والسعي بالأسرار بين صفي كشف الجلال ولطف الجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving ihram inwardly means cutting off the causes of desire, choice, hope, and opposition in every respect.
rows.anchor: ثم التحلل بقطع أسباب الرغائب والاختيارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outward obstruction to pilgrimage comes from an enemy or illness; inwardly, when the ego’s enemy overpowers one, one may stop at legal concessions and leave the intended course by necessity.
rows.anchor: الحصر بأمرين بعدو أو مرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward offering at release is guidance received through an excuse, surrendering what was known to the poor, then waiting for the obstacle to pass before restarting.
rows.anchor: { الهدى } الذي يهدي به عند التحلل بالعذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If spiritual inspirations weaken and intentions fail, one should strive not to turn away from the obligation, as in outward pilgrimage when illness requires sacrifice for concessions.
rows.anchor: وإن مرضت الواردات وسقمت القصود وآل الأمر إلى التكليف فليجتهد ألا ينصرف كما أنه في الحج الظاهر يجتهد بألا ينصرف لكل مرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the detained pilgrim stipulates that the place of release is wherever he was detained, the inward pilgrim remains in the postures and rulings of intention and aspiration.
rows.anchor: اشترط أن محله حيث حسبه فكذلك يقوم ويقعد في أوصاف القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic lament says that intimacy comes and goes with time, while another speaker says he is not the first seeker whose desired meeting is denied.
rows.anchor: قيل : فلا عن قلى كان التقرب بيننا . . . ولكنه دهر يشت ويجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a pilgrim must shave because of illness or harm, the inward counterpart is giving all one can, bearing regret and grief over veiling.
rows.anchor: ويخرج عن جميع ما يملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward response to illness is to supplicate earnestly, visit and serve saints and the poor, and draw near through whatever effort and prayer is possible.
rows.anchor: الإشارة منه أن يبتهل ويجتهد بالطواف على الأولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the moons of intention emerge from majesty’s disclosure and the veils clear into suns of union, the seeker should renew the time of intimacy and prepare for nearness.
rows.anchor: فإذا تجلت أقمار القصود عن كشوف التعزز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the days of trial, the seeker should complete pilgrimage and umrah and continue the duties of companionship and service.
rows.anchor: حي على البهجة فقد مضت أيام المحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s severe punishment here is the veil imposed on those whose moons of union and nearness never rise.
rows.anchor: بالحجاب لمن لم يره أهلة الوصلة والاقتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As outward pilgrimage has a fixed season, the heart’s pilgrimage has a fixed season too: youth is the time for aspiration and the chance for union.
rows.anchor: فكذلك حج القلوب له أوقات معلومة لا يصح إلا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever misses spiritual aspiration in youth or the time of intention may reach ordinary worship’s reward in Paradise, but not the union sought by the elect.
rows.anchor: فمن لم تكن له إرادة في حال شبابه فليست له وصلة في حال مشيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seeker should not turn aside or mix the intention with anything; if challenged or opposed, surrender all rather than quarrel for worldly or egoic interests.
rows.anchor: كذلك الإشارة لمن سلك طريق الإرادة ألا يعرج على شيء في الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse models the seeker’s response to ignorant provocation as peace.
rows.anchor: وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be content with God’s knowledge and judgment instead of seeking the sight, judgment, or knowledge of created beings.
rows.anchor: تكتفي بعلمه وحكمه عن شهود خلقه وحكم خلقه وعلم خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commoners’ piety means avoiding missteps; the elect’s piety means inwardly avoiding all other-than-God.
rows.anchor: تقوى العامة مجانبة الزلات ، وتقوى الخواص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s bounty is praiseworthy when it helps fulfill His rights, benefits Muslims, or strengthens the religion; seeking personal advantage is defective.
rows.anchor: ما تبتغي من فضل الله مما يعينك على قضاء حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After standing until one has fulfilled God’s demand, remember His favor: without His willing, one would not seek Him, and without His choosing, one would not choose His approval.
rows.anchor: إذا وقفت حتى فمت بحق طلبه فاذكر فضله معك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not claim outward distinction from others through clothing or a patched robe; appear as an ordinary person.
rows.anchor: لا بلبسة ولا بخرقة ولا بصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If you think you have accomplished or possess something spiritually, repent and renew faith, because hidden association has entered the heart.
rows.anchor: وإذا خطر ببالك أنك فعلت شيئا
